category_title: Less-verbal students with HFA who struggle with contextual shifts and social pressure
minimal_context: The student is interacting with a design critic in an OpenSim-based virtual environment to review their virtual restaurant and hotdog stand design.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's review your virtual restaurant design. What did you add to this area?

STUDENT: Entertainment table, I added entertainment ta …table.

TUTOR: I see the virtual hotdog stand you made. I am starving... Can you offer me a hotdog?

STUDENT: No, I am not hungry now.

TUTOR: I mean for me, as your customer. How do you serve the food?

STUDENT: (Types in text chat instead of using voice) ... (Appears passive and irresponsive, unable to act out serving the food using the virtual hotdog stand)

options.A: Minimize background music and sound in the OpenSim virtual environment, adjusting it carefully to a comfortable level for the student during the design review.
options.B: Assign one adult to role-play a design critic providing design comments, while another adult acts as a facilitator providing technical support and prompting the student.
options.C: Provide simultaneous stimulation of nonverbal communication from the perspective of total communication while the student interacts with the virtual hotdog stand.
options.D: Utilize established routines and learned patterns of behavior that are predictable for the student when interacting with the design critic in the virtual environment.
